title.zh: 卷464 列傳二百五十一 李端棻 徐致靖子 仁铸 陈宝箴 黄遵宪 曾鉌 杨深秀 杨锐 刘光第 谭嗣同附：唐才常 林旭 康广仁
title.en: Volume 464 Biographies 251: Li Duanfen, Xu Zhijingzi, Ren Zhu, Chen Baozhen, Huang Zunxian, Ceng He, Yang Shenxiu, Yang Rui, Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong with: Tang Caichang, Lin Xu, Kang Guangren
title.raw: 卷464 列傳二百五十一 李端棻 徐致靖子 仁铸 陈宝箴 黄遵宪 曾鉌 杨深秀 杨锐 刘光第 谭嗣同附：唐才常 林旭 康广仁

sentences.zh: 李端棻 徐致靖（子仁鑄） 陳寶箴 黃遵憲 曾鉌 楊深秀 楊銳 劉光第 譚嗣同 唐才常 林旭 康廣仁 李端棻 ，字，人。

translations.literal: Li Duanfen, Xu Zhijing (with his son Ren Zhu), Chen Baozhen, Huang Zunxian, Ceng He, Yang Shenxiu, Yang Rui, Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, Tang Caichang, Lin Xu, and Kang Guangren. Li Duanfen, courtesy name Biyuan, was a native of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Duanfen, Xu Zhijing (and his son Ren Zhu), Chen Baozhen, Huang Zunxian, Ceng He, Yang Shenxiu, Yang Rui, Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, Tang Caichang, Lin Xu, and Kang Guangren. Li Duanfen, whose courtesy name was Biyuan, came from Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，為大學士、尚書所器。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a junior compiler in the Hanlin Academy, appointed compiler, and was esteemed by Grand Secretary Wo Ren and Minister Luo Dunyan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Guangxu reign he took his jinshi degree, entered the Hanlin as a junior compiler, received appointment as a compiler, and won the regard of Grand Secretary Wo Ren and Minister Luo Dunyan.

sentences.zh: 十年，出督學政。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he went out as educational commissioner for Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was sent out to serve as educational commissioner of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 值寇亂後，荒服道亙，前使者試未遍，始一一按臨，文化漸振。

translations.literal: It came after the Muslim rebellion; the frontier roads were cut off, and the previous commissioner had not been able to hold examinations everywhere. Duanfen now went to each place in turn, and culture gradually revived.
translations.idiomatic: This was after the Muslim uprising, when frontier routes were still broken and the previous commissioner had not been able to hold examinations throughout the province. Duanfen now toured each district in person, and learning gradually revived.

sentences.zh: 五年，轉御史，以叔父官京尹，迴避，改故官。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to censor; because his uncle served as metropolitan magistrate of Beijing, he withdrew on grounds of conflict of interest and returned to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made a censor, but when his uncle became metropolitan magistrate of Beijing he withdrew on account of the kinship rule and resumed his former office.

sentences.zh: 累擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to junior grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to junior grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十八年，遷刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was moved to vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 越六年，調倉場。

translations.literal: Six years later he was transferred to the grain depots.
translations.idiomatic: Six years later he was reassigned to oversee the grain depots.

sentences.zh: 前後迭司文柄，四為鄉試考官，一為會試副總裁，喜獎拔士類。

translations.literal: Before and after he repeatedly held control of literary examinations: four times as examiner for the provincial examinations and once as associate chief examiner for the metropolitan examination; he delighted in rewarding and promoting men of talent.
translations.idiomatic: On several occasions he held charge of the civil examinations, serving four times as provincial examiner and once as associate chief examiner for the metropolitan examination, and he took pleasure in recognizing and advancing promising scholars.

sentences.zh: 典試，賞才，以從妹妻之，自是頗納議，娓娓道東西邦制度。

translations.literal: When he presided over the Guangdong examination he admired Liang Qichao's talent, gave him his cousin in marriage, and from then on often accepted Liang's views, discoursing at length on the institutions of Eastern and Western countries.
translations.idiomatic: While conducting examinations in Guangdong he admired Liang Qichao's ability, married him to a cousin by marriage, and thereafter often took Liang's counsel, speaking at length about the political systems of East and West.

sentences.zh: 維時上書請變法，兼及興學。

translations.literal: At that time Kang Youwei memorialized the throne requesting reform, including also the promotion of schools.
translations.idiomatic: About this time Kang Youwei submitted memorials calling for reform and for the expansion of education.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，遂疏請立京師大學，凡各省府、州、縣遍設學堂，分齋講習；

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year Duanfen memorialized requesting the establishment of a national university at the capital, schools throughout every province, prefecture, and county, and separate halls for instruction;
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year Duanfen memorialized to establish a national university in the capital and schools in every province, prefecture, and county, with separate halls for study;

sentences.zh: 並建藏書樓、儀器院、譯書局，廣立報館，選派遊歷生。

translations.literal: and also to build libraries, instrument halls, and translation bureaus, to establish newspapers widely, and to select and send students abroad for observation.
translations.idiomatic: and to set up libraries, instrument halls, and translation bureaus, to open newspapers widely, and to select students to travel abroad for study.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，密薦及堪大用。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he secretly recommended Kang Youwei and Tan Sitong as fit for great employment.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he secretly recommended Kang Youwei and Tan Sitong as men capable of high responsibility.

sentences.zh: 又以各衙門則例，語涉紛歧，疏請刪訂，上尤善之，詔趣各長官定限期革前敝。

translations.literal: He also noted that the regulations of the various yamens were worded in conflicting ways and memorialized requesting their revision; the emperor especially approved this and ordered each chief official to set a deadline for abolishing former abuses.
translations.idiomatic: He further observed that the regulatory precedents of the various offices were inconsistent in wording and asked that they be revised; the emperor was especially pleased and ordered each department head to fix a deadline for removing old abuses.

sentences.zh: 擢禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted to minister of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 未幾，等敗，自疏檢舉，詔褫職，戍。

translations.literal: Before long Kang Youwei and his associates were ruined; Duanfen memorialized accusing himself, and an edict stripped him of office and sent him into exile on the Xinjiang frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Kang Youwei's party fell; Duanfen submitted a memorial denouncing himself, and an edict removed him from office and banished him to Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 中道遘疾，留。

translations.literal: On the way he fell ill and was detained at Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill en route and was held at Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，赦歸，主講。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was pardoned and returned home, where he served as lecturer at the Jingshi Academy in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he was amnestied and went home, where he lectured at the Jingshi Academy in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year he died.

sentences.zh: 元年，從、京朝官請，復官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong, at the request of officials from Yunnan and Guizhou in the capital, his former rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Xuantong reign, at the petition of Yunnan and Guizhou officials in Beijing, his former office was restored.

sentences.zh: 徐致靖（子仁鑄） ，字，人，寄籍。

translations.literal: Xu Zhijing (with his son Ren Zhu), courtesy name Zijing, was a native of Yixing in Jiangsu, registered by adoption at Wanping.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhijing (and his son Ren Zhu), whose courtesy name was Zijing, came from Yixing in Jiangsu and was registered by adoption at Wanping.

sentences.zh: 二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a junior compiler, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangxu he took his jinshi degree, entered the Hanlin as a junior compiler, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍讀學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to reader-in-waiting in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to reader-in-waiting in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 父憂服闋，二十三年，起故官。

translations.literal: When his mourning for his father was completed, in the twenty-third year he was recalled to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: After completing mourning for his father, in the twenty-third year he was recalled to his former office.

sentences.zh: 嘗憂外患日迫，思所以為獻納計。

translations.literal: Zhijing had long worried that foreign danger was pressing daily and thought how he might offer counsel to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijing had long been troubled by the daily tightening of foreign pressure and pondered how he might advise the throne.

sentences.zh: 子，時以編修督學，倡新學，書告舉。

translations.literal: His son Ren Zhu, then serving as compiler and educational commissioner of Hunan, advocated the new learning and wrote urging his father to recommend Kang Youwei.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ren Zhu, then a compiler serving as Hunan's educational commissioner, promoted the new learning and wrote urging his father to recommend Kang Youwei.

sentences.zh: 遂上言：「國是未定，請申乾斷示從違。

translations.literal: Zhijing thereupon memorialized: "The national policy is not yet settled; I beg that Your Majesty's own decision be made clear, showing what is to be followed and what rejected."
translations.idiomatic: Zhijing then memorialized: "The nation's course is still unsettled; I ask that Your Majesty's own judgment be made explicit, showing what is to be adopted and what rejected."

sentences.zh: 」藉以覘上意。

translations.literal: Thus he sought to gauge the emperor's mind.
translations.idiomatic: In this way he hoped to discern the emperor's intentions.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔果求通才，於是奏堪大用，並及、等。

translations.literal: Before long an edict indeed called for men of outstanding ability; Zhijing then memorialized that Kang Youwei was fit for great employment, and also named Liang Qichao, Huang Zunxian, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict did call for men of talent; Zhijing then reported that Kang Youwei was fit for high office, and also named Liang Qichao, Huang Zunxian, and others.

sentences.zh: 又連上書請廢製藝，改試策論，省冗官，酌置散卿。

translations.literal: He also submitted successive memorials requesting the abolition of the examination essay, replacement by policy discourse, reduction of superfluous offices, and the considered establishment of honorary grand secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent a series of memorials asking to abolish the eight-legged essay, test policy essays instead, cut redundant offices, and appoint honorary grand secretaries as appropriate.

sentences.zh: 復以邊患棘，宜練重兵，力荐主軍事。

translations.literal: He further argued that with border troubles acute, heavy troops should be trained and strongly recommended Yuan Shikai to take charge of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He further urged that with border crises pressing, large forces should be drilled, and he strongly recommended Yuan Shikai to direct military affairs.

sentences.zh: 上皆然其言，敕依行。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all his proposals and ordered them carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all his proposals and ordered them implemented.

sentences.zh: 罷斥禮部尚書等阻遏言路，遂命權右侍郎。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Xu Yingkui and others who blocked the channels of remonstrance were dismissed, and Zhijing was ordered to act as acting right vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Xu Yingkui and others who had obstructed memorials to the throne were removed, and Zhijing was appointed acting right vice minister.

sentences.zh: 二十四年八月，太后復出訓政，參預新政諸臣皆獲罪。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twenty-fourth year the empress dowager resumed regency, and all the officials who had taken part in the new policies were punished.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the twenty-fourth year the empress dowager resumed control of government, and every official who had joined the reform movement was punished.

sentences.zh: 褫職坐系，尋定永遠監禁，亦罷官。

translations.literal: Zhijing was stripped of office and imprisoned; soon he was sentenced to perpetual confinement, and Ren Zhu was also dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijing was stripped of rank and imprisoned; he was soon sentenced to lifelong detention, and Ren Zhu was dismissed from office as well.

sentences.zh: 庚子，聯軍陷京師，始出獄待罪，詔赦免。

translations.literal: In the gengzi year, when the allied armies took the capital, he was released from prison to await judgment, and an edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: In the year 1900, when the allied armies occupied Beijing, he was released from prison to await sentence, and an edict granted him amnesty.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 陳寶箴 ，字，人。

translations.literal: Chen Baozhen, courtesy name Youming, was a native of Yining in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Baozhen, whose courtesy name was Youming, came from Yining in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 少負志節，詩文皆有法度，為所器。

translations.literal: From youth he possessed firm resolve; his poetry and prose were all well ordered, and he was esteemed by Zeng Guofan.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed strong character; his poetry and prose were disciplined, and Zeng Guofan valued him.

sentences.zh: 以舉人隨父治鄉團，禦寇。

translations.literal: As a provincial graduate he followed his father Wei Lin in organizing local militia to resist the Cantonese rebels.
translations.idiomatic: While still a provincial graduate he followed his father Wei Lin in raising local militia against the Taiping rebels from Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 已而走，參戎幕，軍、間。

translations.literal: He then went to Hunan, joined Yi Peishen's military staff, and campaigned between Laifeng and Longshan.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Hunan, entered Yi Peishen's staff, and fought between Laifeng and Longshan.

sentences.zh: 來犯，軍飢疲，走募糧，糧至不絕，守益堅，寇稍稍引去。

translations.literal: When Shi Dakai attacked, the army was hungry and weary; Baozhen went to Yongshun to raise grain, supplies arrived without cease, the defense grew firmer, and the rebels gradually withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Dakai attacked, the troops were hungry and exhausted; Baozhen went to Yongshun to raise grain, supplies kept coming, the defense held firm, and the rebels slowly drew off.

sentences.zh: 之，為畫策殲寇，事寧，敘知府，超授。

translations.literal: Baozhen went to Jiangxi, devised plans for Xi Baotian to destroy the bandit Hong Fuzhen; when the affair was settled he was recorded for appointment as prefect and was promoted beyond the regular sequence to Hebei Circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangxi he helped Xi Baotian plan the destruction of Hong Fuzhen's band; when peace returned he was recommended for prefect and was promoted out of turn to intendant of Hebei Circuit.

sentences.zh: 創，遴選三州學子，延名師教之。

translations.literal: He founded the Zhiyong Jingshe Academy, selected students from three prefectures, and invited famous teachers to instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: He founded the Zhiyong Jingshe Academy, chose students from three prefectures, and brought in distinguished teachers.

sentences.zh: 遷按察使，坐事免。

translations.literal: He was transferred to judicial commissioner of Zhejiang and was dismissed because of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was made judicial commissioner of Zhejiang but was removed after an offense.

sentences.zh: 巡撫薦其才，十六年，召入都，除按察使，署布政使。

translations.literal: The Hunan governor recommended his talent; in the sixteenth year he was summoned to the capital, appointed judicial commissioner of Hubei, and given acting charge as provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: The Hunan governor praised his ability; in the sixteenth year he was called to the capital, appointed judicial commissioner of Hubei, and named acting provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 二十年，擢直隸布政使，入對，時東戰亟，見上形容憂悴，請日讀，以期變不失常。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was promoted to provincial treasurer of Zhili; on audience the Sino-Japanese war was urgent, and seeing the emperor's haggard look he asked that he read daily the Kangxi Emperor's imperially approved commentary on the Book of Changes, so that amid change he might not lose constancy.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was promoted to treasurer of Zhili; when he was received in audience the war with Japan was pressing, and seeing how worn the emperor looked he urged daily reading of the Kangxi Emperor's commentary on the Book of Changes so that amid upheaval he might keep his balance.

sentences.zh: 他所陳奏語甚多，並稱旨。

translations.literal: His other memorial statements were numerous, and all pleased the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: His other memorials were many, and all met with the emperor's approval.

sentences.zh: 上以為忠，命治糈台，專摺奏事。

translations.literal: The emperor regarded him as loyal and ordered him to manage the grain depots and submit memorials on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged him loyal and put him in charge of the grain depots with authority to submit memorials directly.

sentences.zh: 成，泣曰：「殆不國矣！

translations.literal: When the Treaty of Shimonoseki was concluded, he wept and said: "The state is nearly lost!"
translations.idiomatic: When the Treaty of Shimonoseki was signed, he wept and said, "The dynasty is all but finished!"

sentences.zh: 」 明年，以薦，擢巡撫。

translations.literal: The next year, on Rong Lu's recommendation, he was promoted to governor of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, on Rong Lu's recommendation, he was made governor of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 撫幕有者，植黨私利，至即重治之。

translations.literal: In the governor's secretariat there was Ren Lin, who formed a faction for private profit; as soon as Baozhen arrived he punished him severely.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Ren Lin in the governor's staff had built a clique for private gain; Baozhen punished him severely as soon as he took office.

sentences.zh: 布政使為關說，據以上聞，獲譴。

translations.literal: The Zhili provincial treasurer Wang Lian interceded for him; Baozhen reported the facts to the throne, and Wang was punished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili treasurer Wang Lian pleaded on Ren's behalf; Baozhen reported the matter upward, and Wang was censured.

sentences.zh: 覆按被劾事，盡暴其任用非人狀，遂褫職。

translations.literal: He reinvestigated the case in which Shi Nianzu had been impeached, fully exposing how Nianzu had employed unworthy men, and Nianzu was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: He reviewed the impeachment of Shi Nianzu, fully exposing how Nianzu had appointed unfit men, and Nianzu was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 繇是有伉直聲。

translations.literal: From this he gained a reputation for stern uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: From this he gained a reputation for uncompromising integrity.

sentences.zh: 俗故闇僿，思以一隅致富強，為東南倡，先後設電信，置小輪，建製造槍彈廠，又立保衛局、、。

translations.literal: Hunan custom was formerly benighted and crude; Baozhen wished to make one corner rich and strong and be a leader for the southeast. In succession he set up telegraph lines, introduced steam launches, built a factory for manufacturing firearms and ammunition, and also established a Public Security Bureau, the Southern Study Society, and the Current Affairs Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan had long been backward and insular; Baozhen hoped to make the province a model of wealth and strength for the southeast. He set up telegraph lines, introduced steam launches, built an arms and ammunition factory, and founded a Public Security Bureau, the Southern Study Society, and the Current Affairs Academy.

sentences.zh: 延主學，俗大變。

translations.literal: He invited Liang Qichao to direct Hunan learning, and local custom changed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He invited Liang Qichao to lead Hunan's schools, and local attitudes changed dramatically.

sentences.zh: 又疏請釐正學術及練兵、籌款諸大端，上皆嘉納，敕令持定見，毋為浮言動，並特旨褒勵之。

translations.literal: He also memorialized requesting correction of scholarship and the major tasks of drilling troops and raising funds; the emperor approved all and ordered him to hold firm views and not be moved by loose talk, and also issued a special edict praising him.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized on reforming scholarship, drilling troops, and raising revenue; the emperor approved everything, told him to stand by his convictions and ignore loose talk, and issued a special edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 是時負盛名，司道咸屏息以伺。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Zhidong enjoyed great fame, and all the circuit intendants and prefects held their breath watching him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhidong then enjoyed enormous prestige, and every provincial official watched him in silence.

sentences.zh: 初綰籓，遇事不合，獨與爭無私撓，雖不懌，無如何也。

translations.literal: When Baozhen first held the Hubei governorship they disagreed on affairs, but he alone contended with Zhang without private bias; though Zhang was displeased, he could do nothing about it.
translations.idiomatic: When Baozhen first governed Hubei they often clashed, yet he alone argued with Zhang without private interest; Zhang was displeased but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 久之，兩人深相結，凡條上新政皆聯銜，而撫反不與。

translations.literal: After a long time the two became deeply allied; whenever they memorialized on the new policies they signed jointly, while the Hubei governor Tan Jixun was left out.
translations.idiomatic: In time the two became close allies and co-signed every memorial on the new policies, while Hubei governor Tan Jixun was not included.

sentences.zh: 會言事數見效。

translations.literal: About this time Kang Youwei's memorials repeatedly took effect.
translations.idiomatic: About then Kang Youwei's proposals repeatedly bore fruit.

sentences.zh: 素慕、薦士，因上言、、、佐新政。

translations.literal: Baozhen had long admired Zeng Guofan and Hu Linyi for recommending talent; he therefore memorialized that Yang Rui, Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, and Lin Xu should assist the new policies.
translations.idiomatic: He had long admired how Zeng Guofan and Hu Linyi had promoted talent, and memorialized that Yang Rui, Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, and Lin Xu should help carry out the reforms.

sentences.zh: 上方詔求通變才，遽擢京卿，參新政，於是四人上書論時事無顧忌。

translations.literal: The emperor had just issued an edict seeking men of adaptable talent; the four were abruptly promoted to grand secretaries in the capital to take part in the new policies, and thereafter they memorialized on current affairs without reserve.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had just called for adaptable talent; the four were suddenly raised to high office in the capital to join the reforms, and from then on they spoke on public affairs without restraint.

sentences.zh: 又言四人雖才，恐資望輕，視事過易，原得厚重大臣如者領之。

translations.literal: Baozhen also said that although the four were talented, their standing might be too slight and they might take office too lightly; he wished that a weighty senior official such as Zhang Zhidong might lead them.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen also said that though the four were able, their rank was low and they might treat office too lightly; he asked that a senior figure such as Zhang Zhidong supervise them.

sentences.zh: 疏上而太后已出訓政，誅四京卿，罪及舉主，去官，其子主事亦革職，並毀學所著、、、諸書。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted the empress dowager had already resumed regency; the four capital grand secretaries were executed, guilt reached the man who had recommended them, Baozhen was removed, his son Sanli, a director in the Secretariat, was also dismissed, and the Hunan school's books Xueyue, Jieshuo, Zhaji, and Dawen were all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the memorial arrived the empress dowager had resumed power; the four capital officials were executed, blame fell on their recommender, Baozhen was dismissed, his son Sanli was stripped of office, and the Hunan school's Xueyue, Jieshuo, Zhaji, and Dawen were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 初，已革道員，以張揭帖攻西教為總督所治。

translations.literal: Earlier, the dismissed circuit intendant Zhou Han of Ningxiang had been punished by the governor for posting broadsheets attacking Western religion.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the dismissed intendant Zhou Han of Ningxiang had been punished by the governor for posting anti-Christian placards.

sentences.zh: 至，復刊帖傳布，令毀之，毆毀帖者，怒，下之獄。

translations.literal: When Baozhen arrived, Zhou Han again printed and distributed placards; Baozhen ordered them destroyed, Zhou Han beat the men who destroyed them, Baozhen was angry, and had him imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Baozhen arrived Zhou Han printed placards again; Baozhen ordered them destroyed, Zhou Han beat those who tore them down, and Baozhen had him jailed in anger.

sentences.zh: 舊黨恨次骨，然喜新之士，亦以此翕然稱之。

translations.literal: The old faction hated him to the marrow, yet men who favored the new learning also united in praising him for this.
translations.idiomatic: The conservative faction hated him bitterly, yet reform-minded men united in praise for the same act.

sentences.zh: 既去，諸所營構便於民者，雖效益已著，皆廢毀無一存雲。

translations.literal: After he left, all the institutions he had built for the people's benefit, though their good effects were already evident, were abolished and destroyed until not one remained.
translations.idiomatic: After he left, every institution he had built for the people, though already proving useful, was abolished until nothing remained.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 黃遵憲 ，字，人。

translations.literal: Huang Zunxian, courtesy name Gongdu, was a native of Jiaying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zunxian, whose courtesy name was Gongdu, came from Jiaying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以舉人入貲為道員。

translations.literal: As a provincial graduate he purchased appointment as a circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: As a provincial graduate he bought appointment as a circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 充使參贊，著上之朝。

translations.literal: He served as attaché on a mission to Japan and presented his Record of Japan to the court.
translations.idiomatic: He served as attaché on the mission to Japan and submitted his Record of Japan to the court.

sentences.zh: 旋移總領事。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to be consul-general at San Francisco.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made consul-general at San Francisco.

sentences.zh: 吏嘗藉口衛生，逮僑滿獄。

translations.literal: American officials once used sanitation as a pretext and arrested Chinese sojourners until the jails were full.
translations.idiomatic: American officials once used public health as a pretext to arrest Chinese residents until the prisons were packed.

sentences.zh: 徑詣獄中，令從者度其容積，曰：「此處衛生顧右於僑居邪？

translations.literal: Zunxian went straight to the prison and ordered his attendants to measure its capacity, saying: "Is sanitation here really better cared for than in the Chinese quarter?"
translations.idiomatic: Zunxian went straight to the jail and had his attendants measure its space, saying, "Is sanitation really better here than where the Chinese live?"

sentences.zh: 」吏謝，遽釋之。

translations.literal: The American officials apologized and released them at once.
translations.idiomatic: The officials apologized and released them immediately.

sentences.zh: 歷鹽法道，署按察使。

translations.literal: He served as salt controller of Changbao Circuit and acted as judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as salt controller of Changbao Circuit and acted as judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時為巡撫，行新政，首倡民治於眾曰：「亦自治其身，自治其鄉而已。

translations.literal: At that time Chen Baozhen was governor and was carrying out the new policies; Zunxian first advocated popular self-government to the crowd, saying: "It is only to govern oneself and to govern one's own township."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Baozhen was then governor and pursuing reforms; Zunxian first preached popular self-government to the people, saying, "It means governing yourself and governing your own township."

sentences.zh: 由一鄉推之一縣、一府、一省，以迄全國，可以成共和之郅治，臻大同之盛軌。

translations.literal: From one township extend it to one county, one prefecture, one province, and then to the whole country, and one may attain the highest government of a republic and reach the great path of universal harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Extend that from one township to a county, a prefecture, a province, and then the whole country, and you can reach the ideal of republican government and the great harmony of the Datong age.

sentences.zh: 」於是略仿西國巡警之制，設保衛局，凡與民利民瘼相麗，而為一方民力能舉者，悉屬之，領以民望，而官輔其不及焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon, roughly imitating the Western police patrol system, he established the Public Security Bureau; all matters touching the people's benefit and hardship that the local people had strength to undertake were placed under it, led by men of local standing, while officials assisted where they fell short.
translations.idiomatic: He then roughly copied the Western police system and set up a Public Security Bureau; everything touching local welfare that the people could manage was placed under respected local leaders, with officials helping where needed.

sentences.zh: 尋解職，奉出使之命，未行而黨禍起，遂罷歸。

translations.literal: Soon he left office, received orders to go abroad as envoy, but before he departed the factional disaster broke out and he returned home dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He soon left office, was ordered abroad as envoy, but before he could depart the reform purge began and he went home.

sentences.zh: 著有等。

translations.literal: His writings include Renjinglu Shicao and others.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote works including Renjinglu Shicao and others.

sentences.zh: 曾鉌 ，字，氏，正白旗人。

translations.literal: Ceng He, courtesy name Huaiqing, of the Xitala clan, was a Bannerman of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Ceng He, whose courtesy name was Huaiqing, of the Xitala clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 父，將軍。

translations.literal: His father Qing Yun was general at Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qing Yun was general at Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 以任子為工部主事，累遷郎中，充軍機章京，轉御史。

translations.literal: By hereditary privilege he became a director in the Ministry of Works, was promoted in succession to bureau director, served as a clerk in the Grand Council, and was transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: By hereditary privilege he entered the Ministry of Works as a director, rose to bureau director, served on the Grand Council staff, and became a censor.

sentences.zh: 九年，出為督糧道。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he went out as grain transport commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was sent out as grain transport commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 、各屬農民納糧例繳省倉，道塗艱遠，多弊竇，設法清釐之，民稱便。

translations.literal: In Xi'an and Tongzhou circuits the peasants were required by custom to deliver grain tax to the provincial granary; the roads were long and hard and there were many abuses; he devised methods to clear them up, and the people called it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xi'an and Tongzhou circuits peasants normally paid grain tax to the provincial granary; the routes were long and corrupt; he reformed the system and the people welcomed the change.

sentences.zh: 士風樸僿，藝事苦窳，延、主書院，督課實學，士論翕然。

translations.literal: The scholarly custom of the Three Assistants region was plain and crude, and the arts were badly neglected; he invited Bo Jingwei of Chang'an and Liu Guangzan of Xianyang to direct the Guanzhong Academy, supervised practical learning, and scholarly opinion united in approval.
translations.idiomatic: Scholarship in the capital region was plain and the arts neglected; he brought Bo Jingwei of Chang'an and Liu Guangzan of Xianyang to head the Guanzhong Academy, stressed practical studies, and scholars rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 又設蠶桑局，聘織師教以煮湅織染法，歲出絲帛埒、。

translations.literal: He also established a sericulture bureau, hired weaving masters to teach boiling, reeling, weaving, and dyeing, and each year the silk and cloth produced rivaled Qi and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He also set up a sericulture bureau, hired weavers to teach reeling, weaving, and dyeing, and each year's silk output rivaled Shandong and Henan.

sentences.zh: 十三年，遷按察使。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was made judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明年，母憂解職。

translations.literal: The next year, on his mother's death, he left office for mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 服除，起故官，俄遷布政使。

translations.literal: When mourning was completed he was recalled to his former post and soon promoted to provincial treasurer of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he returned to office and was soon made treasurer of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，調，迴避，留本任。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to Zhili but withdrew on grounds of conflict of interest and remained in his present post.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to Zhili but stayed in Gansu on account of a conflict-of-interest rule.

sentences.zh: 擢巡撫，慨然曰：「時艱至此，猶可拘成法不變耶？

translations.literal: He was promoted to governor of Hubei and said with emotion: "The times are hard to this degree—can we still cling to established rules and not change?"
translations.idiomatic: He was made governor of Hubei and said with feeling, "Times are this desperate—can we still cling to old rules and refuse to change?"

sentences.zh: 」於是假總督印上陳補官、掣籤、度支、訟獄四事，宜變通成例，厚植國本。

translations.literal: Thereupon, using the Shaan-Gan governor-general's seal, he memorialized on four matters—filling offices, drawing lots for assignment, revenue, and litigation—that established precedents should be flexibly changed to strengthen the foundations of the state.
translations.idiomatic: He then used the Shaan-Gan governor-general's seal to memorialize on filling offices, drawing lots for posts, revenue, and litigation, urging flexible change to strengthen the state.

sentences.zh: 侍讀學士、光祿寺少卿彈其亂政，詔褫職。

translations.literal: Reader-in-waiting Yi Gu and vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Zhang Zhongxin impeached him for disordering government, and an edict stripped him of office.
translations.idiomatic: Reader-in-waiting Yi Gu and vice minister Zhang Zhongxin impeached him for subverting government, and he was dismissed by edict.

sentences.zh: 始，官京朝，家綦貧，僦居陋室。

translations.literal: At first, when Ceng He served in the capital, his family was extremely poor and he rented a mean dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: When he first served in Beijing his family was very poor and he lived in rented quarters.

sentences.zh: 及任外台，孜孜民事，不顧問有無。

translations.literal: When he came to hold a provincial appointment, he worked diligently at the people's affairs, without regard to whether he himself had enough or not.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held office in the provinces, he devoted himself tirelessly to the people's affairs, heedless of his own comfort.

sentences.zh: 既閒廢，出入皆徒步，民恆歲醵金濟之。

translations.literal: After he was dismissed and idle, he went in and out everywhere on foot; the people of Shaanxi regularly pooled money each year to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: After his dismissal he went everywhere on foot; the people of Shaanxi regularly collected money each year to support him.

sentences.zh: 後益困，至敝衣鬻卜都市。

translations.literal: Later his straits grew worse, until he wore tattered clothes and sold divination in the capital markets.
translations.idiomatic: His circumstances worsened until he wore threadbare clothes and sold divination in the city markets.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒。

translations.literal: Before long, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 改元，總督為奏復原官。

translations.literal: At the change of reign era, the governor-general memorialized to restore his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: At the Xuantong change of reign era, Governor-General Duan Fang memorialized to restore his former rank.

sentences.zh: 楊深秀 ，字，本名，人。

translations.literal: Yang Shenxiu, courtesy name Yicun, original name Yuxiu, was a native of Wenxi, Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shenxiu, whose courtesy name was Yicun and whose original name was Yuxiu, came from Wenxi in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 少穎敏，諳西算術。

translations.literal: In youth he was keen and quick, and well versed in Chinese and Western mathematics.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was sharp and quick-witted, and thoroughly versed in Chinese and Western mathematics.

sentences.zh: 初，以舉人入貲為刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: At first, in the early Tongzhi reign, as a provincial graduate he purchased appointment as an assistant department director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tongzhi reign, as a provincial graduate he bought appointment as an assistant department director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 假歸，值大饑，銜命籌賑，條上改革差徭法，困少蘇。

translations.literal: On leave at home, he encountered a great famine; Yan Jingsming, entrusted with the mission to organize relief, submitted a detailed plan reforming the system of corvée and labor levies, and the people's hardship was somewhat eased.
translations.idiomatic: While on leave he encountered the great famine in Shanxi; Yan Jingsming, charged with organizing relief, submitted a detailed plan to reform corvée and labor levies, and the people's distress was somewhat relieved.

sentences.zh: 十五年，成進士，就本官遷郎中，轉御史。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Guangxu he passed the jinshi examination, was transferred in his original post to department director, and then to censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Guangxu he took his jinshi degree, was promoted within his existing office to department director, and then transferred to censor.

sentences.zh: 嘗言：「時勢危迫，不革舊無以圖新，不變法無以圖存。

translations.literal: He once said: "The times are perilously urgent; without reforming the old there is no means to plan the new, and without changing the laws there is no means to plan survival.
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "The times are perilously urgent: without overturning the old there is no way to plan the new, and without changing the laws there is no way to plan for survival."

sentences.zh: 」 二十四年，人脅割、。

translations.literal: " In the twenty-fourth year, the Russians coerced the cession of Port Arthur and Dalian Bay.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, Russia coerced China into ceding Port Arthur and Dalian Bay.

sentences.zh: 深秀力請聯、拒之，詞甚切直。

translations.literal: Shenxiu urgently petitioned to join with Britain and Japan in resisting, his language very forceful and direct.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxiu urgently petitioned that China ally with Britain and Japan to resist, in language that was forceful and blunt.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷銳意行新政，而大臣恆多異議。

translations.literal: At the time the court was keen to carry out new policies, but senior ministers often had many objections.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then eager to enact new policies, but senior ministers constantly raised objections.

sentences.zh: 乃與先後疏請定國是，又以取士之法未善，請參酌、、舊制，釐正文體，下其議於禮部，尚書心非之，未奏也。

translations.literal: He therefore joined Xu Zhijing in successive memorials asking that the national course be fixed; moreover, because the method of selecting talent was not good, he asked that the old systems of Song, Yuan, and Ming be consulted and weighed, the literary forms corrected and standardized, and the discussion sent down to the Ministry of Rites—but Minister Xu Yingkui disapproved in his heart and did not memorialize it.
translations.idiomatic: He and Xu Zhijing then submitted successive memorials asking that the national course be fixed; finding the method of selecting talent inadequate, he urged that the old systems of Song, Yuan, and Ming be consulted, literary forms standardized, and the matter referred to the Ministry of Rites—but Minister Xu Yingkui privately disapproved and never forwarded the proposal.

sentences.zh: 會議經濟特科務減額，於是合彈其阻撓。

translations.literal: When the economic special examination was under discussion with efforts to reduce quotas, he and Song Bolu jointly impeached Xu for obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: When the economic special examination came up for discussion with efforts to cut its quotas, he joined Song Bolu in impeaching Xu Yingkui for obstruction.

sentences.zh: 上令自陳，奏上，劾​​夤緣要津，請罷斥，詞連，上不之詰也。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Xu to explain himself; when the memorial came up, Xu impeached Kang Youwei for currying favor at key posts of power and asked that he be dismissed, implicating Shenxiu in the wording, but the Emperor did not investigate Shenxiu.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Xu Yingkui to explain himself; in his reply Xu impeached Kang Youwei for currying favor at key posts and asked that he be dismissed, implicating Shenxiu in the wording—but the Emperor did not pursue Shenxiu.

sentences.zh: 御史劾傳布有為所立，並暴交通內外狀，責以代人報復，反獲咎。

translations.literal: Censor Wen Ti impeached Shenxiu for spreading the Society for the Preservation of the Nation established by Youwei, and exposed Youwei's communications inside and outside the court; Emperor Dezong rebuked Wen for retaliating on another's behalf, and Wen himself incurred blame.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wen Ti impeached Shenxiu for disseminating the Baoguo Society founded by Kang Youwei and exposed Youwei's dealings inside and outside the court; Emperor Dezong rebuked Wen for retaliating on another's behalf, and Wen himself was punished.

sentences.zh: 益感奮，連上書請設譯書局，派王公遊歷各國，並定遊學章程，皆報可。

translations.literal: Shenxiu was all the more inspired, and in successive memorials asked that a Translation Bureau be established, that princes and nobles be sent to tour various countries, and that regulations for study abroad in Japan be fixed—all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxiu was all the more stirred to action, and in a series of memorials asked that a Translation Bureau be established, that princes and nobles be sent to tour foreign countries, and that regulations for study in Japan be drawn up—all were approved.

sentences.zh: 又請試庶官，日番二十人，料簡貞實，而汰其庸愚罷老不諳時務者，繇是廷臣益側目。

translations.literal: He also asked to test ordinary officials, twenty per day in rotation, to select the upright and sincere and eliminate the mediocre, foolish, worn out, and aged who did not understand current affairs; from this court ministers looked upon him with ever greater resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed testing ordinary officials twenty at a time each day, selecting the upright and sincere while weeding out the mediocre, foolish, and aged who did not understand current affairs; from this the court ministers looked upon him with growing hostility.

sentences.zh: 巡撫圖治甚急，中蜚語，為剖辨之，上以特旨褒，乃得行其志。

translations.literal: The Hunan governor Chen Baozhen was extremely eager to govern; malicious rumors spread against him, and Shenxiu clarified matters in his defense. The Emperor issued a special edict praising Baozhen, and only then was Baozhen able to carry out his aims.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan Governor Chen Baozhen was pressing hard for reform when slander spread against him; Shenxiu defended him in a memorial, and the Emperor issued a special edict praising Baozhen, who was then able to carry out his plans.

sentences.zh: 八月，政變，舉朝惴惴，懼大誅至，獨抗疏請太后歸政。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the coup occurred; the whole court was fearful, dreading mass executions—Shenxiu alone submitted a bold memorial asking the Empress Dowager to restore the Emperor to power.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the coup occurred; the whole court trembled, fearing mass executions—yet Shenxiu alone submitted a bold memorial asking the Empress Dowager to restore power to the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 方疏未上時，其子苦口諫止，厲聲叱之退。

translations.literal: Just as the memorial had not yet been submitted, his son Futian bitterly remonstrated to stop him; Shenxiu sharply rebuked him and ordered him to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Before the memorial could be submitted, his son Futian pleaded desperately with him to desist; Shenxiu sharply rebuked him and ordered him away.

sentences.zh: 俄被逮，論棄市。

translations.literal: Soon he was arrested and sentenced to execution in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was arrested and condemned to execution in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 性鯁直，嘗面折人過，以此叢忌。

translations.literal: By nature he was blunt and upright; he would often rebuke people to their faces over their faults, and for this many bore grudges against him.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was blunt and upright, often rebuking others to their faces over their faults—and for this he accumulated many enemies.

sentences.zh: 官臺諫十閱月，封事二十餘上，稿不具存，惟獄中詩三章流傳於世。

translations.literal: In ten months as a remonstrance official on the censorate, he submitted more than twenty sealed memorials; the drafts are not fully preserved—only three poems from prison circulate in the world.
translations.idiomatic: In ten months on the censorate he submitted more than twenty sealed memorials; the drafts are not fully preserved—only three poems written in prison survive.

sentences.zh: 著有、。

translations.literal: His works include Collected Drafts from the Hall of Empty Sounds and the New Gazetteer of Wenxi County.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Collected Drafts from the Hall of Empty Sounds and the New Gazetteer of Wenxi County.

sentences.zh: 楊銳 ，字，人。

translations.literal: Yang Rui, courtesy name Shujiao, was a native of Mianzhu, Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rui, whose courtesy name was Shujiao, came from Mianzhu in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 少俊慧，督學奇其才，招入幕。

translations.literal: In youth he was handsome and clever; educational commissioner Zhang Zhidong marveled at his talent and recruited him into his staff.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was brilliant and quick-witted; Educational Commissioner Zhang Zhidong was struck by his talent and brought him onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 肄業，年最少，嘗冠其曹。

translations.literal: He studied at the Zunjing Academy; though the youngest in years, he often led his class.
translations.idiomatic: He studied at the Zunjing Academy; though the youngest in his cohort, he often ranked first among his peers.

sentences.zh: 優貢朝考得知縣。

translations.literal: As an outstanding tribute student he passed the metropolitan tribute examination and was appointed district magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as an outstanding tribute student, he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed district magistrate.

sentences.zh: 督，從赴。

translations.literal: When Zhidong became governor-general of the Two Guang, Rui followed him to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zhidong became governor-general of the Two Guang, Rui accompanied him to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 十一年，舉順天鄉試，考取內閣中書。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Guangxu he passed the Shuntian provincial examination and was selected as a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Guangxu he passed the Shuntian provincial examination and was selected as a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，薦應經濟特科。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, through recommendation he was entered for the economic special examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year Zhang Zhidong recommended him to sit for the economic special examination.

sentences.zh: 又以薦，與、、並加四品卿，充軍機章京，參新政。

translations.literal: Again through Chen Baozhen's recommendation, he was together with Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, and Lin Xu promoted to fourth-grade secretary, appointed Grand Council clerk, and assigned to participate in the new policies.
translations.idiomatic: Again through Chen Baozhen's recommendation, he was together with Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, and Lin Xu promoted to fourth-grade secretary, appointed Grand Council clerk, and charged with carrying out the new policies.

sentences.zh: 召見，面陳興學、練兵為救亡策，稱旨。

translations.literal: Summoned for audience, Rui stated face to face that promoting learning and drilling troops were the strategies to save the state—the Emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When summoned for audience, Rui stated directly that promoting education and drilling troops were the strategies to save the nation—and the Emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 七月，禮部主事上封事，尚書等格不奏。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Ministry of Rites clerk Wang Zhao submitted a sealed memorial, but Minister Xu Yingkui and others blocked it from being memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, Ministry of Rites clerk Wang Zhao submitted a sealed memorial, but Minister Xu Yingkui and others withheld it from the throne.

sentences.zh: 上聞，震怒，盡褫尚書侍郎六人革職，朝臣皆不自安。

translations.literal: When the Emperor learned of it, he was furious and stripped all six ministers and vice ministers of their posts; court officials were all ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor learned of this he was furious and dismissed all six ministers and vice ministers; the court was thrown into unease.

sentences.zh: 上手詔密諭云：「近日朕仰觀聖母意旨，不欲退此老耄昏庸大臣而進英勇通達之人，亦不欲將法盡變。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally issued a secret hand-edict to Rui, saying: "Recently I have looked up to observe the Empress Dowager's intent: she does not wish to remove these aged, senile, and incompetent ministers and advance brave and penetrating men, nor does she wish to change the laws entirely.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor personally sent Rui a secret hand-edict: "Of late I have observed the Empress Dowager's intent—she does not wish to remove these aged and incompetent ministers in favor of bold and capable men, nor does she wish to change the laws entirely.

sentences.zh: 朕豈不知積弱不振，非力行新政不可？

translations.literal: Do I not know that China has long been weak and failing, and that vigorous new policies are indispensable?
translations.idiomatic: Do I not know that China has long been weak and enfeebled, and that only vigorous new policies can save it?

sentences.zh: 然此時不惟朕權力所不及，若強行之，朕位且不能保。

translations.literal: Yet at this time not only is my power insufficient; if I force matters, I cannot even keep my throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at this moment my power does not reach that far; if I force the matter, I cannot even keep my throne.

sentences.zh: 爾與、、等詳悉籌議，必如何而後能進用英達，使新政及時舉行，又不致少拂聖意，即具奏，候朕審擇，不勝焦慮之至！

translations.literal: You and Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, Lin Xu, and the others should deliberate thoroughly on how brave and able men may be advanced so that the new policies may be carried out in good time, yet without the least offense to the Empress Dowager's wishes—memorialize at once, and I shall examine and choose. I am unspeakably anxious!
translations.idiomatic: You, together with Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, Lin Xu, and the others, must deliberate carefully on how to advance able men so that the new policies may proceed in good time without the least offense to the Empress Dowager's wishes—memorialize at once for my review. My anxiety is beyond words!"

sentences.zh: 」復奏言：「太后親挈大位授之皇上，皇上宜以孝先天下，遇事將順。

translations.literal: Rui memorialized again: "The Empress Dowager personally invested the great throne in Your Majesty; Your Majesty should put filial piety before all under Heaven and accommodate her wishes in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Rui memorialized in reply: "The Empress Dowager personally invested the throne in Your Majesty; Your Majesty should put filial piety before all else and accommodate her wishes in every matter.

sentences.zh: 變法宜有次第，進退大臣不宜太驟。

translations.literal: Reform should proceed in due order; advancing and dismissing ministers should not be too abrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Reform should proceed step by step; the advancement and dismissal of ministers should not be too sudden."

sentences.zh: 」上是之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 已而太后再訓政，諸言新政者皆予重誅。

translations.literal: Before long the Empress Dowager again assumed regency; all who spoke for the new policies were given severe punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Empress Dowager resumed regency, and all who had advocated the new policies were severely punished.

sentences.zh: 既下獄，自揣實無罪，謂即訊不難白，次日，遽詔與等同棄市。

translations.literal: Once Rui was imprisoned, he reckoned himself truly guiltless and thought that under interrogation he could easily clear himself—but the next day an edict suddenly ordered him executed in the marketplace together with Guangdi and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Once imprisoned, Rui believed himself innocent and thought he could easily clear his name under interrogation—but the next day an edict suddenly ordered him executed in the marketplace together with Liu Guangdi and the others.

sentences.zh: 改元，子繳手詔於都察院，請代奏，始傳於世。

translations.literal: At the Xuantong change of reign era, Rui's son Qingchang submitted the hand-edict to the Censorate and asked that it be memorialized on his behalf; only then did it circulate in the world.
translations.idiomatic: At the Xuantong change of reign era, Rui's son Qingchang submitted the hand-edict to the Censorate and asked that it be forwarded to the throne; only then did it become known to the world.

sentences.zh: 劉光第 ，字，人。

translations.literal: Liu Guangdi, courtesy name Peicun, was a native of Fushun, Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guangdi, whose courtesy name was Peicun, came from Fushun in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 九年進士，授刑部主事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Guangxu he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Guangxu he took his jinshi degree and was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 治事精嚴，因讞獄忤長官​​，遂退而閉戶勤學，絕跡不詣署。

translations.literal: In handling affairs he was meticulous and strict; because of a criminal case he offended his superior, whereupon he withdrew, closed his doors, and studied diligently, cutting off all visits to the yamen.
translations.idiomatic: He handled business with exacting rigor; when a criminal case brought him into conflict with his superior, he withdrew, shut his doors to study, and stopped going to the office altogether.

sentences.zh: 家素貧，而性廉介，非舊交，雖禮饋弗受。

translations.literal: His family had long been poor, yet his nature was upright and incorruptible; unless they were old friends, he would not accept gifts even of courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: His family had always been poor, but he was incorruptible by nature and would accept no courtesy gift from anyone who was not an old friend.

sentences.zh: 獨與善。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Yang Rui alone.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rui alone numbered among his close friends.

sentences.zh: 通、及。

translations.literal: He was versed in the Offices of Zhou, the Rites, and the Record of Rites of the Elder and Younger Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply versed in the Offices of Zhou, the Rites, and both recensions of the Record of Rites.

sentences.zh: 其應召也，亦以薦，然非其素志，將具疏辭，人官京朝者力勸之。

translations.literal: When he answered the summons, it was also on Chen Baozhen's recommendation; yet this was not his original intent—he was about to prepare a memorial declining—but Sichuan officials serving in the capital strongly urged him on.
translations.idiomatic: He answered the summons on Chen Baozhen's recommendation too, though it was not what he had wanted; he was preparing a memorial to decline when Sichuan colleagues in the capital pressed him hard to accept.

sentences.zh: 一日，召見，力陳時危民困，外患日迫，亟宜虛懷圖治，上稱善。

translations.literal: One day he was summoned for audience and forcefully stated that the times were perilous, the people distressed, and foreign danger pressing daily; the throne should urgently open its mind and plan good government—the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: One day he was received in audience and spoke urgently of national peril, popular distress, and the daily tightening of foreign pressure, urging the emperor to govern with an open mind; the emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 惟時言路宏啟，臣民奏事日數百計，竟日批答，簽識可否，以待上裁。

translations.literal: At that time the channels of remonstrance were broadly opened; memorials from officials and commoners numbered hundreds each day; Guangdi spent the whole day drafting responses, marking approval or rejection, awaiting the emperor's final decision.
translations.idiomatic: Memorial channels were then wide open, with hundreds of submissions arriving daily; Guangdi spent entire days drafting replies and marking what should stand or fall, all for the emperor's final ruling.

sentences.zh: 退語所親曰：「吾終不任此，行當亟假歸矣！

translations.literal: On retiring he said to those close to him: "I can never bear this burden—I shall soon ask leave and return home at once!
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he told those close to him, "I cannot carry this burden—I mean to ask leave and go home at once!

sentences.zh: 」未一月而禍作，自投獄。

translations.literal: " Less than a month later disaster struck; he went and surrendered himself to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Less than a month later catastrophe fell, and he surrendered himself to prison.

sentences.zh: 臨刑，協辦大學士監斬，詫曰：「未訊而誅，何哉？

translations.literal: At the execution, Associate Grand Secretary Gang Yi supervised the beheading; Guangdi exclaimed in astonishment: "Execution without interrogation—why?
translations.idiomatic: At the execution Associate Grand Secretary Gang Yi supervised the beheading; Guangdi cried out in astonishment, "To put a man to death without trial—why?

sentences.zh: 」令跪聽旨，不可，曰：「祖制，雖盜賊，臨刑呼冤，當復訊。

translations.literal: " He was ordered to kneel and hear the edict; he refused, saying: "By ancestral institution, even for thieves, if one cries innocence at execution, there should be re-examination.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to kneel and hear the edict; he refused, saying, "By ancestral law, even a thief who cries injustice at execution must be heard again.

sentences.zh: 吾輩縱不足惜，如國體何！

translations.literal: Even if our lives are not worth sparing, what of the dignity of the state!
translations.idiomatic: Even if we are not worth sparing, what becomes of the dignity of the state!

sentences.zh: 」默不應，再詢之，曰：「吾奉命監刑耳，他何知​​？

translations.literal: " Gang Yi remained silent and did not answer; when asked again, he said: "I am only carrying out orders to supervise the execution—what else do I know?
translations.idiomatic: Gang Yi said nothing; pressed again, he replied, "I am here only to supervise the execution on orders—what more do I know?

sentences.zh: 」獄卒強之跪，崛立自如。

translations.literal: " The jailers forced him to kneel, but he stood erect and at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The jailers tried to force him to his knees, but he stood straight and unmoved.

sentences.zh: 呼曰：「，跪！

translations.literal: Yang Rui called out: "Peicun, kneel!
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rui called out, "Peicun, kneel!

sentences.zh: 跪！

translations.literal: Kneel!
translations.idiomatic: Kneel!

sentences.zh: 遵旨而已。

translations.literal: It is only to obey the edict."
translations.idiomatic: It is only to obey the edict."

sentences.zh: 」乃跪就戮。

translations.literal: Then he knelt and submitted to execution.
translations.idiomatic: Then he knelt and went to his death.

sentences.zh: 著有。

translations.literal: His writings include Jiebai Tang shiwenji (Collected Poetry and Prose of the Jiebai Hall).
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Jiebai Tang shiwenji (Collected Poetry and Prose of the Jiebai Hall).

sentences.zh: 譚嗣同（唐才常） ，字，人。

translations.literal: Tan Sitong (with Tang Caichang appended), courtesy name Fusheng, was a native of Liuyang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Sitong (with Tang Caichang appended), whose courtesy name was Fusheng, came from Liuyang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 父，巡撫。

translations.literal: His father Jixun was governor of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tan Jixun was governor of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 少倜儻有大志，文為奇肆。

translations.literal: From youth he was free-spirited and had great ambition; his writing was bold and unconventional.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was spirited and ambitious, and his prose was bold and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 其學以日新為主，視倫常舊說若無足措意者。

translations.literal: His learning took daily renewal as its principle; he regarded conventional morality and old doctrines as scarcely worth a thought.
translations.idiomatic: He took daily renewal as the heart of his learning and treated conventional morality and inherited doctrine as hardly worth notice.

sentences.zh: 素謹飭，以是頗見惡。

translations.literal: Jixun was by nature strict and proper, and for this reason Sitong was much disliked by him.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun was stern and proper by nature, and for this Sitong was much disliked by his father.

sentences.zh: 乃遊幕，以同知入貲為知府，銓。

translations.literal: Sitong then traveled on Liu Jintang's staff in Xinjiang; through purchase of office as sub-prefect he became prefect and was assigned to Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Liu Jintang's staff in Xinjiang, bought appointment as prefect through the rank of sub-prefect, and was assigned to Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 撫，還鄉佐新政。

translations.literal: When Chen Baozhen became governor of Hunan, Sitong returned home to assist the new policies.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Baozhen became Hunan governor he went home to help carry out the reforms.

sentences.zh: 倡辦，為之長。

translations.literal: Liang Qichao advocated establishing the Southern Study Society, and Sitong served as its head.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Qichao founded the Southern Study Society, and Sitong served as its director.

sentences.zh: 屆會期，集者恆數百人，聞慷慨論時事，多感動。

translations.literal: When meetings came due, those assembled were always several hundred; hearing Sitong speak passionately on current affairs, many were moved.
translations.idiomatic: Meetings regularly drew hundreds, and many were moved when they heard Sitong speak passionately about public affairs.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，召入都，奏對稱旨，擢四品卿、軍機章京。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was summoned to the capital; his memorial responses pleased the throne, and he was promoted to fourth-rank grand secretary and clerk in the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was called to the capital; his audience replies pleased the emperor, and he was raised to fourth-rank grand secretary and appointed to the Grand Council staff.

sentences.zh: 四人雖同被命，每召對，建議獨多。

translations.literal: Although all four received the same commission, at each audience Sitong alone offered the most proposals.
translations.idiomatic: All four received the same commission, but at every audience Sitong offered the most proposals.

sentences.zh: 欲開，設顧問官，令擬旨，必載明前朝故事，將親詣請命太后。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to open Maoxun Hall, establish advisory officials, and have Sitong draft edicts—each must clearly cite precedents from past dynasties—and he would personally go to the Summer Palace to request the empress dowager's approval.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor planned to open Maoxun Hall and appoint advisory officials, with Sitong drafting edicts that cited past dynastic precedents, while he himself would go to the Summer Palace to seek the empress dowager's consent.

sentences.zh: 退謂人曰：「今乃知上絕無權也！

translations.literal: Sitong withdrew and said to others: "Now I know the emperor has absolutely no power at all!
translations.idiomatic: On leaving, Sitong told others, "Now I see the emperor has no real power at all!

sentences.zh: 」時督，以監司練兵。

translations.literal: " At that time Rong Lu supervised the metropolitan region, and Yuan Shikai, as surveillance commissioner, drilled troops at Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Lu then supervised the metropolitan region while Yuan Shikai, as surveillance commissioner, drilled troops at Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 詔擢侍郎，召入覲。

translations.literal: An edict promoted Yuan Shikai to vice minister and summoned him for audience.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted Yuan Shikai to vice minister and summoned him to court.

sentences.zh: 嘗夜詣有所議。

translations.literal: Sitong once went by night to Yuan Shikai to discuss certain matters.
translations.idiomatic: Sitong once visited Yuan Shikai at night for a private talk.

sentences.zh: 明日，返天津。

translations.literal: The next day Yuan Shikai returned to Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Yuan Shikai went back to Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 越晨，太后自還宮，收政權。

translations.literal: The following morning the empress dowager returned from the Summer Palace to the palace and seized back governmental power.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning the empress dowager returned from the Summer Palace to the Forbidden City and reclaimed power.

sentences.zh: 避匿日本使館，往見之，勸東遊。

translations.literal: Liang Qichao hid in the Japanese legation; Sitong went to see him, and Liang urged Sitong to flee eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Qichao took refuge in the Japanese legation; Sitong visited him and Liang urged him to flee abroad.

sentences.zh: 曰：「不有行者，無以圖將來；

translations.literal: Sitong said: "Without one who goes, there is no way to plan for the future;
translations.idiomatic: Sitong said, "Without someone who survives to act, there is no way to plan for the future;

sentences.zh: 不有死者，無以酬聖主。

translations.literal: without one who dies, there is no way to repay the sagely sovereign."
translations.idiomatic: without someone who dies, there is no way to repay a devoted sovereign."

sentences.zh: 」卒不去。

translations.literal: In the end he did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he refused to go.

sentences.zh: 未幾，斬於市。

translations.literal: Before long he was beheaded in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 著有及等。

translations.literal: His writings include Renxue (On Benevolence) and Mangcangzhai shiji (Collected Poems of the Mangcangzhai Studio), among others.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Renxue and Mangcangzhai shiji, among other works.

translations.literal: Tang Caichang, courtesy name Fochen.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Caichang, whose courtesy name was Fochen.

sentences.zh: 少與齊名，稱「二生」，高材生也。

translations.literal: From youth he was equally famous with Sitong and was called "the Two Talents of Liuyang"; he was an outstanding student of the Lianghu Academy.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he had ranked equal with Sitong as "the Two Talents of Liuyang," an outstanding student at the Lianghu Academy.

sentences.zh: 聞死，憂憤，屢有所謀，每言及，常泣下。

translations.literal: When he heard of Sitong's death he was anguished and enraged; he repeatedly plotted action, and whenever he spoke of Emperor Guangxu he often wept.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of Sitong's death, he was stricken with grief and rage; he plotted repeatedly, and whenever he spoke of Emperor Guangxu he wept.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，兩宮出狩，陰結謀舉事，號勤王，將攻、。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, when the two sovereigns went on tour, he secretly joined the Fuyou Society to plot an uprising, styled it "Rescue the Throne," and planned to attack Wuhan and Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, after the court fled on tour, he secretly organized the Fuyou Society to raise arms under the banner of "Rescue the Throne," planning to strike at Wuhan.

sentences.zh: 被獲，慷慨言無所隱，請就死，遂殺之。

translations.literal: He was captured; speaking boldly he concealed nothing, asked to die, and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Captured, he spoke without concealment and asked only to die; he was killed.

sentences.zh: 林旭 ，字，人。

translations.literal: Lin Xu, courtesy name Tangu, was a native of Houguan in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Xu, whose courtesy name was Tangu, came from Houguan in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 年十九，舉本省鄉試第一。

translations.literal: At nineteen he placed first in the provincial examination of his province.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he topped the provincial examinations in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 後試禮部，值構釁，糾同試者上書論時事，不報。

translations.literal: Later he sat for the Ministry of Rites examination; when the Sino-Japanese conflict broke out, he joined fellow candidates in memorializing on current affairs, but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: He later took the metropolitan examination; when war broke out with Japan, he joined fellow candidates in a memorial on public affairs, but the court did not reply.

sentences.zh: 入貲為內閣中書。

translations.literal: He purchased appointment as a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He bought appointment as a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時倡言變法，先於京師立，以振厲士氣，而、、、諸會繼之。

translations.literal: At that time Kang Youwei advocated reform; he first established the Guangdong Study Society in the capital to rouse scholarly morale, and the Sichuan, Zhejiang, Shaanxi, and Fujian study societies followed.
translations.idiomatic: When Kang Youwei began calling for reform, he first founded the Guangdong Study Society in the capital to stir scholarly morale; the Sichuan, Zhejiang, Shaanxi, and Fujian societies followed.

sentences.zh: 為領袖，又充會員。

translations.literal: Xu was leader of the Fujian Study Society and also served as a member of the Society for the Preservation of the Nation.
translations.idiomatic: Xu led the Fujian Study Society and also joined the Baoguo Society.

sentences.zh: 先為將軍，雅好士，及至，延入幕。

translations.literal: Rong Lu had earlier been general at Fuzhou and had long favored Fujian scholars; when he reached Tianjin he took Xu into his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Lu, formerly general at Fuzhou, had long favored Fujian scholars; when he went to Tianjin he brought Xu onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 俄以奏保人才召見，操土語，上不盡解。

translations.literal: Soon, on memorial recommendation as talent, Xu was summoned for audience; he spoke in his local dialect and the emperor did not fully understand.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned on memorial recommendation; he spoke in his local dialect and the emperor could not fully follow him.

sentences.zh: 退繕摺，上稱善，遂命與等同參機務，詔諭多起草。

translations.literal: On retiring he revised his memorial; the emperor praised it and ordered him to take part in confidential affairs together with Tan Sitong and the others; many edicts and instructions were drafted by Xu.
translations.idiomatic: He then revised his memorial, which the emperor praised, and was ordered to join Tan Sitong and the others in confidential duties; many edicts were drafted by Xu.

sentences.zh: 及變起，同戮於市，年二十有四。

translations.literal: When the coup broke out he was executed in the marketplace together with the others, at the age of twenty-four.
translations.idiomatic: When the coup came he was executed in the marketplace with the others, aged twenty-four.

sentences.zh: 著有。

translations.literal: His writings include Wancui Xuan shiji.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Wancui Xuan shiji.

sentences.zh: 妻孫女，聞變，仰藥不死，以毀卒。

translations.literal: His wife was a granddaughter of Shen Baozhen; when she heard of the disaster she took poison but did not die, and died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was Shen Baozhen's granddaughter; on hearing the news she took poison but survived, and died of grief.

sentences.zh: 康廣仁 ，名，以字行，弟。

translations.literal: Kang Guangren, personal name Youpu, styled by his courtesy name, was Kang Youwei's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Guangren, whose personal name was Youpu and who went by his courtesy name, was Kang Youwei's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 少從兄學。

translations.literal: From youth he studied under his elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he studied under his brother.

sentences.zh: 上書請改革，謂當先變科舉，庶人才可出。

translations.literal: When Youwei memorialized requesting reform, Guangren said the civil examinations should be changed first, so that talent might emerge.
translations.idiomatic: When Youwei memorialized for reform, Guangren urged that the examinations be changed first so talent could emerge.

sentences.zh: 其後罷鄉會試、製藝，而歲科試未變，激勵言官抗疏論之，得旨俞允。

translations.literal: Thereafter the provincial and metropolitan examinations and the examination essay were abolished, but the annual local examinations were not yet changed; Guangren urged the remonstrance officials to submit bold memorials on this, and the throne assented.
translations.idiomatic: After the provincial and metropolitan examinations and the eight-legged essay were abolished, the annual local tests remained unchanged; Guangren pressed censors to memorialize boldly, and the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 於是語：「今科舉既廢，宜且南歸興學專教育，俟養成多數有用才，數年後乃可云改革也。

translations.literal: Guangren then said to Youwei: "Now that the examinations are abolished, you should return south for a time and devote yourself to education, wait until many useful men have been trained, and only after several years speak again of reform."
translations.idiomatic: Guangren then told Youwei, "With the examinations gone, you should go south and devote yourself to education, train many useful men, and only after several years speak of reform again."

sentences.zh: 」不忍去。

translations.literal: Youwei could not bear to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Youwei could not bring himself to leave.

sentences.zh: 及初聞變，復趣歸。

translations.literal: When the coup was first heard of, Guangren again urged Youwei to return home.
translations.idiomatic: When news of the coup first came, Guangren again urged Youwei to flee.

sentences.zh: 走，被逮。

translations.literal: Youwei fled; Guangren was arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Youwei escaped; Guangren was arrested.

sentences.zh: 在獄言笑自若，臨刑猶言曰：「自強之機在此矣！

translations.literal: In prison he spoke and laughed as usual; at execution he still said: "China's opportunity for self-strengthening lies here!"
translations.idiomatic: In prison he was calm and even cheerful; at the block he still said, "China's chance to strengthen itself lies in this!"

sentences.zh: 」 【論曰】 論曰：戊戌變法，發憤圖強，用等言，召用新進。

translations.literal: The commentator says: The commentator says: In the Wuxu reforms Emperor Dezong, stirred to strengthen the state, followed the counsel of Li Duanfen and others and summoned new men.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: In the Wuxu reforms Emperor Dezong, determined to strengthen the state, took the advice of Li Duanfen and others and called in new men.

sentences.zh: 百日維新，外震仰，黨爭遽起，激成政變。

translations.literal: For a hundred days the new policies awed China and the world alike, but factional struggle broke out at once and provoked the coup.
translations.idiomatic: For a hundred days the reforms awed China and the world, but factional struggle erupted and provoked the coup.

sentences.zh: 、、、及、同日被禍，世稱「六君子」，皆悲其志。

translations.literal: Rui, Guangdi, Sitong, Xu, together with Shenxiu and Guangren, suffered execution on the same day; the world called them the "Six Gentlemen," and all mourned their purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Rui, Guangdi, Sitong, Xu, Shenxiu, and Guangren were executed on the same day; the world called them the Six Gentlemen, and all mourned their purpose.

sentences.zh: 內爭不已，牽及外交。

translations.literal: Internal strife did not cease, and foreign relations were drawn into it.
translations.idiomatic: Internal strife continued and entangled foreign relations.

sentences.zh: 其後遂釀庚子排外之亂，終致危亡。

translations.literal: Thereafter the Boxer uprising of 1900 was brewed, and in the end the dynasty was brought to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: This led to the Boxer uprising of 1900 and, in the end, ruin.

sentences.zh: 此亦代興衰一大關鍵也。

translations.literal: This too was a great turning point in the rise and fall of the Qing.
translations.idiomatic: This was a great turning point in the fate of the Qing dynasty.
